deep.reconstruction:
Folio 161r is written upside down relative to the scan; rotated by 180° it reads normally. It contains no formulas, derivations, figures or computations. All of it is pencil Kurrent prose: one dense block of about 12 heavily corrected lines with many strike-throughs and interlinear insertions, a few isolated short lines, and a separate block of 3–4 lines with a word underlined by a brace.

The few fragments I can read are tentative. Among them are "die ganze Abhandlung" and "ich unterlasse". There may also be a mention of "Weierstrass", a reference to an earlier part ("Theil") of the Abhandlung, and to lectures ("Vorlesungen") or Göttingen; these readings are uncertain.

The surrounding pages show what this is. The previous page drafts the topological preliminaries of the 1857 paper: a closed surface T cut by 2p cross-cuts into a simply connected T*, and the constancy of the jumps of a function across each cross-cut. The next page drafts the opening of "Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen" (Crelle 54, 1857). That draft says the paper treats Abelian functions by a method whose principles were set out in his dissertation and in three short preliminary papers, and refers to his Göttingen lectures of Michaelis 1855–1856.

This page therefore almost certainly belongs to the same drafting of prefatory or historical remarks for the 1857 paper. The most plausible content, which is my inference and not a verified reading, is a draft of Riemann's remark on the history and priority of the theta-inversion part of his work. That remark mentions his 1855/56 lectures and Weierstrass's Crelle papers on hyperelliptic and Abelian inversion (vol. 47, 1854, with the fuller treatment announced in vol. 52). It also contains a phrase of the type "ich unterlasse", i.e. Riemann declining to go into some point.

No mathematical derivation is present that could be restated in modern notation.
